paragraphs.title: A Corrupt Society and the Loss of Integrity

easy.explanation: Micah says, “The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men.”
easy.q: What does Micah say about good and upright people in the land?

answers: They lie in wait for blood and hunt one another
easy.explanation: The people lie in wait for blood and hunt every man his brother with a net.
easy.q: What do people do to one another?

easy.explanation: The passage says that a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.
easy.q: What problem is found within the families?

answers: The land is full of fruit
The prophet seeks good people but finds none
The prophet wants to leave the land
medium.explanation: Like a person looking for fruit but finding no cluster, Micah finds almost no good or upright people.
medium.q: What does the search for summer fruit and grapes represent?

answers: The judge refuses to hear cases
The prince and judge seek rewards
medium.explanation: The prince asks and the judge asks for a reward, showing that money influences judgment.
medium.q: What causes justice to be corrupted?

answers: The judge is influenced by payment
The judge seeks peace between the parties
The judge follows an ancient law
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates bribery or payment affecting the judge’s decision.
medium.q: What does “asketh for a reward” mean in this context?

answers: Trust has broken down even within the home
challenge.explanation: The corruption is so deep that people must guard their words even with those closest to them.
challenge.q: Why does Micah warn people not to trust even close companions?

answers: Both arise from dishonesty and broken trust
challenge.explanation: Violence, bribery, and dishonesty destroy trust in government and eventually in family relationships.
challenge.q: How are public corruption and family division connected?

answers: The people are fruitful and mature
Even the best people are dangerous and corrupt
The people are weak like grass
challenge.explanation: The best of the people are compared to a brier, and the upright to a sharp thorn hedge.
challenge.q: What does the image of the brier and thorn hedge communicate?

short_answers.question: What does Micah desire when he looks for the firstripe fruit?
short_answers.answer: He desires to find good and upright people, but none can be found.
short_answers.explanation: The missing fruit symbolizes the lack of righteous people.

short_answers.question: What do the prince and judge seek?
short_answers.answer: They seek a reward or payment.
short_answers.explanation: Their desire for payment corrupts justice.

short_answers.question: Who are described as a man’s enemies?
short_answers.answer: The men of his own house.

paragraphs.title: Hope in God and Rising After the Fall

easy.explanation: Micah says, “I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation.”
He declares, “When I fall, I shall arise.”
easy.q: What will happen after Micah falls?

easy.explanation: Micah says, “When I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.”
easy.q: What will the LORD be to the one sitting in darkness?

answers: He acknowledges his sin and waits for judgment and salvation
He wants to take revenge himself
He does not believe God will hear him
medium.explanation: Micah says he has sinned and will wait until the LORD pleads his cause and executes judgment.
medium.q: Why is Micah willing to bear the indignation of the LORD?

answers: She will see her downfall and be ashamed
medium.explanation: The enemy will be covered with shame and trodden down like the mire of the streets.
medium.q: What will happen to the enemy who mocks Israel?

medium.explanation: Micah bears the LORD’s indignation, meaning His righteous anger, because he has sinned.
medium.q: What does “indignation” mean in this passage?

answers: Falling and rising, darkness and light
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts falling with rising and darkness with the LORD’s light.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in Micah’s words?

answers: Micah expects God to judge his cause and bring him into the light
Salvation comes without regard to anything
challenge.explanation: Micah waits for God to plead his cause, execute judgment, and bring him to the light.
challenge.q: How are judgment and salvation connected?

answers: The enemy trusts only in her own power
The enemy already recognizes God’s power
challenge.explanation: The question is a boastful mockery of Israel’s faith.
challenge.q: What does the enemy’s question, “Where is the LORD thy God?” reveal?

short_answers.question: For whom does Micah wait?
short_answers.answer: He waits for the LORD, the God of his salvation.
short_answers.explanation: Micah expresses confidence that God will hear him.

short_answers.question: What happens when Micah sits in darkness?
short_answers.answer: The LORD becomes a light unto him.
short_answers.explanation: God’s presence gives hope in distress.

short_answers.question: What will happen to the mocking enemy?
short_answers.answer: She will be covered with shame and trodden down.
short_answers.explanation: Her mockery will end in humiliation.

paragraphs.title: A Day of Judgment Against the Enemy

easy.explanation: The verse says, “In the day that thy walls are to be built.”
easy.q: What will be built on the day described?

answers: It will be filled with fruit
easy.explanation: The land shall be desolate because of the deeds of its inhabitants.
easy.q: What will happen to the land?

answers: Because of the fruit of the people’s doings
easy.explanation: The passage directly connects the desolation with the fruit of their doings.
easy.q: Why will the land become desolate?

answers: The event is limited to one city
The event extends across a broad region
The people remain inside their homes
medium.explanation: The many places named emphasize a wide geographical scope.
medium.q: What does the list of Assyria, fortified cities, rivers, seas, and mountains suggest?

answers: The established order or boundary will be changed
Nothing will change in the future
medium.explanation: The phrase follows the rebuilding of walls and the movement of peoples, suggesting altered boundaries or conditions.
medium.q: What does “the decree be far removed” suggest in the context?

medium.explanation: Desolate means devastated, abandoned, or barren.

answers: As a quick restoration of the enemy
As a judgment that prevents easy recovery
As an event with no earthly result
challenge.explanation: The passage describes changed boundaries and desolation rather than an easy recovery.
challenge.q: How is the day of judgment portrayed in relation to the enemy’s recovery?

answers: The land suffers because of the evil deeds of its inhabitants
The land is punished without cause
challenge.explanation: The land becomes desolate because of the fruit of their doings.
challenge.q: What moral principle appears in verse 13?

answers: The enemy’s mockery is followed by judgment and humiliation
Israel stops waiting for the LORD
challenge.explanation: After the enemy is shamed, the passage describes judgment and desolation.
challenge.q: How does this section connect with the preceding passage about the enemy?

short_answers.question: What is to be built on the appointed day?
short_answers.answer: The walls are to be built.
short_answers.explanation: The rebuilding of the walls marks a significant change.

short_answers.question: From where will people come according to the passage?
short_answers.answer: They will come from places including Assyria, fortified cities, the river, seas, and mountains.
short_answers.explanation: The list emphasizes the broad reach of the event.

short_answers.question: What causes the land to become desolate?
short_answers.answer: The fruit of the doings of those who dwell in it.
short_answers.explanation: Their actions bring the land’s desolation.

paragraphs.title: A Prayer for Israel’s Restoration and Exodus-like Wonders

easy.explanation: Micah asks, “Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage.”
easy.q: What image does Micah use when appealing to God for the people?

easy.explanation: The people are asked to feed in Bashan and Gilead.
easy.q: Which regions are named as places of pasture?

answers: The days of Israel’s coming out of Egypt
easy.explanation: God promises to show wonders according to the days of the Exodus.
easy.q: To which time does Micah compare the wonders he requests?

answers: God should lead, protect, and care for His people
The people should leave their land
medium.explanation: The image presents Israel as God’s heritage needing His care and guidance.
medium.q: What does the shepherd-and-flock image express?

answers: They are pasturelands to which the people are asked to return
They are places where the enemy is hiding
They are symbols of desolation only
medium.explanation: The passage asks that the flock feed in these former grazing regions.
medium.q: Why are Bashan and Gilead mentioned?

medium.explanation: Marvellous things are remarkable acts of divine power.

answers: Both express divine leadership and deliverance
challenge.explanation: Shepherding represents God’s care, while the Exodus represents His miraculous deliverance.
challenge.q: How are shepherding and the memory of the Exodus related?

answers: Complete restoration, including security and miraculous intervention
An end to Israel’s relationship with God
challenge.explanation: The prayer asks both for safe provision and for renewed divine wonders.
challenge.q: What hope arises from the movement from pasture to wonders?

answers: Israel belongs to God and needs His care
Israel should scatter among its enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the people as God’s own flock.
challenge.q: What does “the flock of thine heritage” emphasize?

short_answers.question: How does Micah describe the people?
short_answers.answer: He describes them as the flock of God’s heritage.
short_answers.explanation: The shepherd image portrays God’s ownership and care.

short_answers.question: Where should the flock feed?
short_answers.answer: In Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
short_answers.explanation: These regions represent restored pasture and security.

short_answers.question: What does God promise to show?
short_answers.answer: He promises to show marvellous things like those associated with the Exodus.
short_answers.explanation: The Exodus becomes the model for future wonders.

paragraphs.title: The Humbling of the Nations and Their Fear of God

answers: Only the strength of the walls
easy.explanation: The nations will see God’s power and be confounded at their own might.

answers: Lay a hand upon their mouth
easy.explanation: They shall lay their hand upon their mouth.
easy.q: What will they do with their hands?

easy.explanation: They shall be afraid of the LORD and fear because of Him.

answers: Their power will prove useless before God’s power
medium.explanation: God’s power will expose the weakness of their own strength.
medium.q: Why will the nations be ashamed of their might?

medium.explanation: The gesture represents stunned silence before God’s greatness.
medium.q: What does putting a hand upon the mouth suggest?

medium.explanation: Licking dust is an image of abasement and defeat.
medium.q: What does licking the dust like a serpent represent?

answers: They move from boasting to silence, trembling, and fear
They move from weakness to victory
They move from celebration to feasting
challenge.explanation: They are confounded, silent, shaken, and afraid before the LORD.
challenge.q: How do the nations move from confidence to fear?

answers: It emphasizes the loss of security and stability
It shows that they are building new homes
It describes their return to power
challenge.explanation: The image portrays frightened creatures leaving their hiding places.
challenge.q: What does moving out of their holes like worms add to the picture?

answers: They recognize the real and visible power of God
They do not know whom to fear
They trust only their own strength
challenge.explanation: Their fear shows recognition of God’s authority and power.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the nations fearing the LORD and fearing because of Him?

short_answers.question: What will the nations do when they see God’s might?
short_answers.answer: They will be confounded and ashamed of their own strength.
short_answers.explanation: God’s power will expose their weakness.

short_answers.question: What physical gesture shows their astonishment?
short_answers.answer: They will lay their hand upon their mouth.
short_answers.explanation: The gesture symbolizes silence and amazement.

short_answers.question: How will the nations respond to the LORD?
short_answers.answer: They will be afraid and fear because of Him.
short_answers.explanation: Their confidence will be replaced by submission.

paragraphs.title: God’s Mercy and the Fulfillment of the Promise to the Ancestors

easy.explanation: The passage asks, “Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity?”
easy.q: What does the LORD pardon or bear away?

answers: Cast them into the depths of the sea
easy.explanation: God will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
easy.q: What will God do with the sins of His people?

answers: Truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham
Truth to Abraham and mercy to Jacob
easy.explanation: The closing verse says God will perform the truth to Jacob and the mercy to Abraham.
easy.q: To whom are truth and mercy connected?

answers: He does not hold His anger forever
medium.explanation: God’s anger is not permanent because He delights in mercy.
medium.q: What does “he retaineth not his anger for ever” teach about God?

answers: Mercy shows God’s faithfulness to His promises
Mercy ends the relationship with the ancestors
medium.explanation: God’s mercy is joined to His keeping of the promises sworn to the fathers.
medium.q: How are mercy and the promise to the ancestors connected?

answers: The deep places of the sea
medium.explanation: The phrase means the deepest parts of the sea and pictures complete removal.
medium.q: What are “the depths of the sea”?

answers: God combines forgiveness, compassion, and covenant faithfulness
challenge.explanation: The ending emphasizes pardon, compassion, the removal of sin, and faithfulness to the fathers.
challenge.q: What is the central idea at the end of the book?

answers: It makes the sins nearby and accessible
It pictures the sins being removed far away
It shows that the sins immediately return
challenge.explanation: The image conveys deep and complete removal of sin.
challenge.q: How does casting sins into the sea strengthen the idea of forgiveness?

answers: His mercy supports His fulfillment of the promises
His mercy prevents Him from keeping promises
His mercy concerns only Israel’s enemies
challenge.explanation: God’s mercy appears both in forgiveness and in keeping His covenant promises.
challenge.q: How does God’s delight in mercy relate to His oath to the fathers?

short_answers.question: What does God do with iniquity and transgression?
short_answers.answer: He pardons iniquity and passes by transgression.
short_answers.explanation: The passage presents God as merciful and forgiving.

short_answers.question: What does God do with the people’s sins?
short_answers.answer: He casts them into the depths of the sea.
short_answers.explanation: This symbolizes complete removal of their sins.

short_answers.question: What will God perform to Jacob and Abraham?
short_answers.answer: He will perform the truth to Jacob and the mercy to Abraham.
short_answers.explanation: He remains faithful to the promises sworn to the ancestors.
